title: Basic Text Styling ✍️
description: Control font family, size, weight, alignment, spacing, and decoration.

slides.title: Font Family 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦
slides.content:
# Choosing Typefaces

`font-family` sets the typeface. Provide a comma‑separated list as a fallback system:

```css
body {
  font-family: 'Open Sans', Arial, sans-serif;
}
```
- First choice: 'Open Sans' (if installed or loaded via Google Fonts).
- Fallback: Arial (if Open Sans isn't available).
- Generic family: sans-serif (browser's default sans‑serif font).

Always end with a generic family (`serif`, `sans-serif`, `monospace`, `cursive`, `fantasy`).

slides.title: Font Size & Weight 📏
slides.content:
# Control Size and Boldness

- `font-size` accepts values in `px`, `em`, `rem`, `%`, and keywords (`small`, `large`).
  ```css
  h1 { font-size: 2.5rem; }
  p { font-size: 16px; }
  ```
- `font-weight` sets the thickness: `normal`, `bold`, `lighter`, `bolder`, or numeric values (100–900).
  ```css
  strong { font-weight: 700; }
  ```

`rem` (root em) is relative to the root `<html>` font size; it's great for scalable typography.

quizData.question: What does `font-size: 2em;` mean?

options.text: Twice the size of the parent element's font size

quizData.explanation: `em` is relative to the font size of the element's parent.

slides.title: Text Alignment & Spacing 📐
Text Decoration & Transform 🔗
slides.content:
# Underline, Overline, Uppercase

- `text-decoration` – `underline`, `overline`, `line-through`, `none` (often used to remove underlines from links).
- `text-transform` – `uppercase`, `lowercase`, `capitalize`.
- `font-style` – `normal`, `italic`, `oblique`.
- `font-variant` – `small-caps`.

Shorthand `font` can combine many of these:
```css
p {
  font: italic small-caps bold 16px/1.5 'Open Sans', sans-serif;
}
```

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use Web Fonts

Services like Google Fonts let you include custom fonts by adding a `<link>` in your HTML or an `@import` in CSS. This expands your typography beyond basic system fonts.
